symptom: Block processing panics with an out-of-bounds index (major, 1 instance, crackmes.one 629a286b33c5d45b75903c7a MSVC i386 PE thief_crackme.exe, sub_41cd08 @0x41cd08)

witness.before: exit 1; substrate/block.rs:648 panicked 'index out of bounds: the len is 1 but the index is 1'; decompile-all recorded a WARNING stub
witness.after: exit 0; 21 lines of C (the three xchg-decodes, the swi(4) and the ret-8 tail)

decisions: The filed hypothesis ('an unchecked block invariant fails on the protected instruction stream') and the round-3 refutation are both UPHELD, and the invariant is now named: a basic block's MULTIEQUALs carry one input per in-edge in edge order, and the resync that keeps that true is Funcdata::branchRemoveInternal.

The refuter's correction (1) is confirmed: nothing about this is specific to a protected instruction stream. The path is generic unreachable-block removal and the packer only supplies the dead-block shape. It is measured on 17 unrelated challenge images.

The refuter looked at the unreachable arm of block_remove_internal, which skips the push_multiequals + per-out-edge resync the !unreachable arm does. That arm is innocent. Measured with a per-action scan for 'a MULTIEQUAL preceded by a non-MULTIEQUAL in the same block': the layout is already broken immediately after the `stackptrflow` action, long before remove_unreachable_blocks runs, and a scan at the top of remove_unreachable_blocks reports it clean while a scan after the edge-sever loop reports blk 2 with size_in=1 and two phis of arity 2.

The creator is ActionStackPtrFlow::analyzeExtraPop (coreaction.cc:303-320, kuna p6_variables/coreaction_stackptr.rs:763), which rewrites a solved MULTIEQUAL into an INT_ADD **in place** -- it does not move the op out of the marker run. op_zero_multi does the same MULTIEQUAL->COPY. So the 'MULTIEQUALs are one contiguous leading run' invariant that branchRemoveInternal's `break` depends on is not one. On the witness the block's op list is [MULTIEQUAL, INT_ADD@41cd57, MULTIEQUAL, MULTIEQUAL, INT_ADD, ...] and the sweep patched 1 phi of 3.

Fixed by scanning the target's whole op list for the opcode instead of breaking at the first non-marker -- which is exactly what block_remove_internal already does, in kuna AND in upstream C++ (funcdata_block.cc:272 uses `continue` where :213 uses `break`). On a well-formed block the two spellings visit the identical set of phis, so the change is a no-op wherever the invariant holds; that is why the datatest and decbench corpora do not move.

The refuter's correction (2) -- that the acceptance probe cannot tell a fix from a cover-up, because a bounds guard or a clamp at block.rs:648 would also make it exit 0 while emitting a phi with a dropped or mis-wired input -- drove the shape of the fix and the evidence. This is NOT a guard: the stale slot is removed, the phi collapses to a COPY of the value the surviving edge carries, and descend2_undef never sees the phi at all, so no 0xBADDEF is interposed. Evidence is a whole-corpus before/after diff of the emitted C, classified per function, not the absence probe.

Not gated behind a phases.toml option, per the captain's T_TRIAGE instruction and docs/agents.md: a panic that yields a WARNING stub instead of C is not a judgement call. DIV-159 records the divergence from upstream's `break`.

The alternative fix -- relocating an op out of the marker run when it is converted away from MULTIEQUAL, restoring the invariant at its source -- was rejected for this PR. It would move ops in every function where op_zero_multi fires (which is most of them), so it is a corpus-wide reordering with no witness demanding it; the consumer-side scan is provably zero-diff wherever the invariant already holds.

tests.stage: none -- there is no option, so a two-pass stages XML is not expressible; the invariant is asserted directly by the unit test
tests.fixture: decompiler/crates/kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures/phimarkerrun_pe_i386.exe (+ .py generator): a 5 KiB PE32 mapping the 760-byte protected run at its original address 0x41cd08 into an RWX section

promoted_probe.why: the need's target is binary_source dataset and CI has no dataset. The vendored stub reproduces the identical panic, but only through decompile-all (the whole-binary load is what gives the stub its caller and the stack-solver equation that converts the phi); decompile-all reports the seam on stdout, so the clause moved from stderr_absent to stdout_absent. The need record keeps the dataset acceptance and the --addr spelling so every later B_VERIFY runs the real witness.

ablation.method: two stage. (1) reachability prefilter: an instrumented build reports when the new scan patches a phi the old break would have skipped, run over every image. (2) full before/after `decompile-all` on the survivors plus a random decbench control, unified diff of the emitted C classified per function.
ablation.targets: 975 images -- 803 decbench-dataset binaries (O0/O2/inlined/large/sample-set) + 169 RE-dataset challenge images + 3 others
ablation.decbench_control_ab: 60 random decbench binaries re-run under a full before/after decompile-all: 60/60 byte-identical
ablation.error_stubs: 39 -> 9 across the 17; the 9 survivors fail on a different seam (rename_recurse: set_input_varnode (empty stack)), which is the sibling need ssa-renaming-panics-protected

speed.method: the change adds no work on a well-formed block -- the loop visits the identical set of ops and only the terminator differs (break vs continue over the remaining ops of one block). No timing claim is made because there is no measurable target: 0 of 803 decbench binaries reach the changed branch at all.
